hero.title: Saudi Arabia × Navier — the Kingdom's water-mobility platform
hero.subtitle: PIF is building the coastline of Vision 2030. Navier is the foiling standard that connects it.
hero.what_we_do_together: We make Navier the water-mobility platform across PIF's destinations — NEOM, The Red Sea, AMAALA, Jeddah and the Eastern Province — one software-defined foiling fleet, one operating standard, with a path to in-Kingdom localization. Navier brings the platform and the network playbook proven in the Maldives; PIF brings the destinations, the demand and the Vision-2030 mandate.

partner_context.their_ambition: You are building the giga-project coastline of Vision 2030 — NEOM, The Red Sea, AMAALA, Jeddah Central, and the Eastern Province industrial heartland. Each is a world-class destination on the water, and you own the mandate to choose the platforms that move people across them.
partner_context.their_pressure: These destinations are opening now and need premium, sustainable mobility that matches their ambition — and Vision 2030 rewards local content and job creation, not just imported fleets. The water-mobility standard for the entire Kingdom is being set in your window.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier can be your Saudi water-mobility platform across PIF's assets — one software-defined foiling standard from NEOM to the Red Sea to Jeddah to the Gulf coast — with a Turkey factory that makes regional and in-Kingdom localization credible.

partner_json_extract.why_now: PIF's destinations are opening — The Red Sea is operating, AMAALA is coming online, NEOM is taking shape — and the mobility standard is being set right now. The opportunity is to own the premium, on-demand and long-range layer across all of PIF's coast — not one destination at a time.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging at the islands' excuse. Autonomy is arriving on the water before the road. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

The Red Sea destination -> AMAALA (Triple Bay)

partner_json_extract.multimodal_fit: A single foiling standard across every PIF coastal asset: shared fleet, shared operations, shared certification — connected to each destination's airport, resorts and urban waterfront, and ultimately stitching the Red Sea and Gulf coasts into one network with Quanta-LR range.

differentiation.why_navier: A software-defined, autonomy-ready platform; a Turkey factory that makes in-Kingdom localization (assembly, jobs, Vision-2030 local content) credible for you; and at-scale proof in the Maldives.

proof_points.claim: The platform runs at sovereign scale.
proof_points.evidence: ~100 vessels / $100M / 3-year phasing in the Maldives — 'the playbook to replicate'.
The King Fahd Causeway (Eastern Province ↔ Bahrain) sets record passenger volumes with chronic congestion — a marine alternative is compelling.

objections.response: Navier's existing Turkey factory makes regional supply and a path to in-Kingdom assembly and jobs realistic — local content, not just imports.
Pioneer II (70 nm) covers intra-destination capillaries; Quanta-LR (2,000 nm hybrid) connects The Red Sea↔AMAALA↔NEOM and crosses the Gulf — with no charging-infrastructure dependency.

the_ask.navier_brings: A software-defined foiling platform (Pioneer II + Quanta-LR), the Maldives-proven network playbook, certification, operations, and a path to in-Kingdom localization via the Turkey factory.
the_ask.partner_brings: You bring PIF's destinations and demand, the Vision-2030 mandate, and the coordination across NEOM, Red Sea Global and the Eastern Province.
the_ask.next_step: A platform framework with PIF: a Red Sea + NEOM pilot that sets the Kingdom-wide water-mobility standard.

close.title: One foiling standard for the coastline of Vision 2030.
close.body: The Red Sea and NEOM prove it, Jeddah urbanises it, and the Eastern Province crossing plus Quanta-LR through-runs make it national. Navier as the water-mobility platform of the Kingdom — built, in part, in the Kingdom.
